title: How To Tow Away And Steal ATMs In GTA 6
summary:
There are hundreds of ATMs all over the world of Grand Theft Auto 6. To be fair, you’re not going to withdraw cash from them often, as it’s always better to keep money in your checking account or family savings account. So, if you don’t plan on withdrawing money, then perhaps you’d much rather steal it. Thankfully, you can do just that by using tow trucks and vans.

In This Article
  • Requirements: Towing vehicle and Dye Pack Jammer
  • How to install the winch
  • Heave-ho! Pulling away the ATM
  • How to destroy stolen ATMs to get cash

Requirements: Towing vehicle and Dye Pack Jammer

If you want to steal ATMs in GTA 6, you need a vehicle that can tow them away and the Dye Pack Jammer to help maximize your take.

When it comes to vehicles, your options include various types of tow trucks or pickup trucks, such as the Bravado Bison 1800 and Vapid Montagne Pickup. There are plenty of these vehicles being driven around by hapless civilians, so just steal one and take it out for a spin.

As for the Dye Pack Jammer, it's a means of countering an anti-theft device:

  • Basically, when an ATM or packets of marked money get stolen, there's a mechanism that releases pink ink.
  • This defaces the bills and makes them useless.
  • You also get covered in a bright color that makes it easier for cops to recognize you.

To offset these issues, you must progress through the campaign until you get the Credit Check main mission in Chapter 3. Complete it to permanently unlock the Dye Pack Jammer, which prevents dye from ruining your robbery efforts.

How to install the winch

The vast majority of pickup trucks and tow trucks lug around trailer implements for tools, boats, and smaller vehicles. You don’t want those. Instead, you must install a winch.

To install a winch, you have to visit a Mod Shop that specializes in that particular type of vehicle. For example, if you have a pickup truck, you need to head to Wasteland Off-road in Kelly County. Likewise, owners of the Ultimate Edition may also head to One-Eyed Willie’s Auto Shop in Leonard County.

Once you’re in the corresponding Mod Shop, go to the Bodyworks - Towing tab and buy the winch upgrade. It costs $1,595.

Heave-ho! Pulling away the ATM

Okay, so you've unlocked the Dye Pack Jammer and you have a viable towing vehicle. Now, you’re ready to steal ATMs in GTA 6. Here's how the process goes:

  • Make your way to an establishment with an ATM--there should be one or two in small towns, usually in areas with convenience stores or restaurants.
  • Similarly, you can open your BuckMe app and select the “Find Nearest ATM” option to mark it on your map.
  • Once you've spotted an ATM, position your vehicle so that the back/winch is facing it, then slowly reverse. You should see the winch automatically latch onto the machine.
  • Drive forward, then reverse, and drive forward again. Keep repeating this a few times until you’re able to pull out the machine from the walls.

Note: This action automatically triggers an alarm, so expect police to show up soon enough.

How to destroy stolen ATMs to get cash

Well, you’re lugging around a huge ATM, while being chased by cops. But you still need to grab the cash from it. There are different methods, so pick one that suits the given situation:

  • Explosives - Evade the cops and look for a safe area. Then, plant a sticky bomb or throw a grenade to blow up the ATM.
  • Cut-off Tool - This is also unlocked during Chapter 3. Complete the Meet the Heders mission to receive a device that lets you cut and saw through locked latches.
  • Vehicular carnage - The last option, simply put, means that you just destroy the ATM by smashing it into cars, walls, and obstacles.

Regardless of the method that you chose to open the ATM, you’ll see four metal lockboxes with dollar signs. Do melee attacks to stomp on them, causing them to spill out their contents. Go ahead and grab the cash on the ground.

You’re going to feel lost as you explore the cities, beachfronts, and seedy underbelly of Leonida. If you need more help navigating the massive game world and tackling its activities, be sure to check our Grand Theft Auto 6 guides hub.

title: All Gym Locations In GTA 6
summary:
In Grand Theft Auto 6, a large emphasis is placed on Jason and Lucia working out and staying in shape. The better shape the characters are in, the higher their stats, which include health, stamina, and focus. So, if you want Jason and Lucia ready to fight enemies and run around Leonida, you need them in peak physical health.

The best way to do that in GTA 6 is by visiting a gym, which you might have seen at Jason's safehouse in Chapter 1. However, following the events of Chapter 1, you'll need a new gym. Unfortunately, they become fairly hard to come by, especially during the earlier parts of the game. To save you time looking around Leonida, we have a full list of every gym location in GTA 6 ready for you in the guide below.

  • How to find every gym in GTA 6
    • Zenith
    • Vice Seven Condominiums Gym
    • Grand Majestic Gym
    • Dynamix Fitness
    • Venus Fitness
    • Ajax Gym/Lawton Theater
    • Muscle Sands
    • Y Hotel Fitness Club
    • Aichi Condominiums Outdoor Gym

How to find every gym in GTA 6

In total, we have been able to find nine gyms across Leonida in GTA 6. This doesn't include Jason's outdoor gym at his Key Lento house.

For the most part, these gyms are located in and around downtown Vice City, as that's where all of the major bodybuilding occurs. You'll find some outdoor gyms, cheaper gyms with few amenities, and multi-level gyms that offer anything from a pool to billiards to a bar to dozens of unique weight-lifting machines and stations.

Below, we'll show you the names, prices, and locations of all nine gyms in GTA 6 so you know exactly where to go to get ripped:

Zenith

  • Location: Just south of downtown Vice City and north of Tequesta
  • Features: Food options and a wardrobe to change clothes
  • Membership fee: $750

Vice Seven Condominiums Gym

  • Location: In the heart of Tequesta, just above the "Tequesta" text on the map
  • Features: None
  • Membership fee: $450

Grand Majestic Gym

  • Location: In south Tequesta and north of Peacock Bay
  • Features: Food options and a billiards table
  • Membership fee: $250

Dynamix Fitness

  • Location: In central Bayside, south of Stockyard and east of La Perle. North of Boobie's apartment in Chapter 3
  • Features: Wardrobe to change clothes
  • Membership fee: $600

Venus Fitness

  • Location: In south Ocean Beach, located south of the central park
  • Features: Wardrobe to change clothes
  • Membership fee: $600

Ajax Gym/Lawton Theater

  • Location: Located just before the highway that connects Oldby Island to Penmarch Isle
  • Features: Food options, a pool, multiple levels of equipment, and a wardrobe to change clothes
  • Membership fee: $1,800 (but also offered for free during the story)

Muscle Sands

  • Location: Located outdoors on the beachfront in east Ocean Beach
  • Features: None
  • Membership fee: $0

Y Hotel Fitness Club

  • Location: In south Washington Beach, east of Oldby Island, northeast of the central park
  • Features: Pool, bar, and food options
  • Membership fee: $1,200 (but also offered for free during the story)

Aichi Condominiums Outdoor Gym

  • Location: Located in north Washington Island, east of Leaf Links, just south of the highway that connects to Flamingo Island
  • Features: None
  • Membership fee: $950

For right now, those are all of the gyms you can join as Jason and Lucia in GTA 6. A couple of the gyms offer you free membership through the main story, so you're wise to wait until then to pay any expensive fees. For the most part, though, all gyms work the same in GTA 6, so you can get shredded at any of them that you choose.

For more on GTA 6, from completing side missions to finding a tricky location on the sprawling map of Leonida, we’ve got you covered with our Grand Theft Auto 6 guides hub.

title: Xbox Project Helix Was Reportedly Designed To Make Online Multiplayer Free
summary:
For years, most multiplayer games on Xbox consoles required a subscription to go online. From Xbox Live to Xbox Game Pass, Microsoft paywalled multiplayer on its platforms, but the company reportedly aimed to break down that barrier for its next-gen console, Project Helix.

According to Windows Central, Project Helix was conceived under the previous Xbox leadership team as the device that would bridge the divide between PC and console gaming. Like the Asus Xbox ROG Ally PC handhelds, the console is said to have an Xbox-inspired interface and full PC game support through storefronts like Steam. Because of that design decision, it's claimed it didn't make sense to continue with paid multiplayer, since that service is free for games purchased on PC platforms like Steam and the Epic Games Store.

As the Windows Central report noted, that was reportedly the plan before Xbox leadership was shaken up and gaming hardware prices rose during the AI boom. With Asha Sharma now in charge of Xbox, the gaming division is more focused on profitability, and Microsoft's gaming arm has seen sweeping changes.

Mass layoffs and studio divestitures occurred throughout 2026, and Project Helix could be a very expensive family of devices. If Microsoft ditches paid multiplayer, it loses a revenue stream for its next-gen push at a time when component prices have risen steeply.

As part of its 25th anniversary celebrations, Microsoft also teased a few more details about Project Helix, calling it specifically "a console" that plays games from your PC, not "a PC that can also play console games."

"When we think about Project Helix, it’s really designed to be the ultimate gaming machine--one that removes all the barriers of play that have historically existed," VP of next-gen Jason Ronald said.

title: GTA 6 Hacker Releases Full Xbox Build, And PC Modders Are Already Trying To Get It Running
summary:
Infamous GTA 6 Leaker Cyberleek resurfaced last week, threatening to release a crucial file for the Xbox build of GTA 6 that could be used to create an unofficial PC port of the game. The hacker originally promised to publicly drop the .exe file for this version of the game depending on whether their memecoin hit a certain market cap, and has been taunting publisher Take-Two Interactive for failing to prevent the game files from leaking online.

"Months of takedowns, subpoenas, and wallet-tracing later, the hunt is still on and the uploads keep arriving," Cyberleek wrote in a now-removed post on Reddit, insisting they were "fighting anti-consumerism" in the video games industry with their actions and using crypto funds to work on a new project. "There is no other way to move funds without names," Cyberleek added. "And this work requires no names."

As pointed out online, Cyberleek has already cashed out on their memecoin in August and again in October, raking in hundreds of thousands of US dollars. So far, it looks like modders are already making modest headway with the full Xbox build of GTA 6, as the Project Leonida Discord server (via Eurogamer) has footage of the game booting up on PC. That's as far as it gets (for now), as that start-up process is met with a black screen shortly afterward. Modders and homebrew enthusiasts are reportedly using Claude AI to reverse-engineer the game on that platform, and the group is confident that a playable build will be ready within a week.

Rockstar has yet to officially announce a PC port of GTA 6, but rumors suggest it could be out in early 2027. This would be a very short gap between console and PC releases for a Rockstar-developed game, as the studio's console-first projects usually spend many months in incubation before heading to PC. The threat of a homebrewed PC port, however, could pressure the developer to release GTA 6 on PC sooner rather than later.

Meanwhile, GTA 6 has done phenomenally well on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S since it launched last week. The game kicked off with 32.5 million copies sold on its first day, and just a few days later, that number reportedly rose to 44.9 million. PS5 sales have dominated, and Sony says GTA 6 was the biggest launch in PlayStation history.

title: Can You Romance Vicki In GTA 6?
summary:
The main story in Grand Theft Auto 6 actively pushes Jason and Lucia into a romantic relationship, even though the player can resist it, if they prefer. However, there are plenty of other side characters that players would like the chance to try to romance, and one character near the top of that list is Vicki.

Similar to Mandy, another potential romance partner in GTA 6, many find Vicki to be an attractive side character who plays a role in the main story. Narratively speaking, Vicki is more of a factor than Mandy, but she shows less romantic interest in either Jason or Lucia. Still, in a game where anything is possible, you might be wondering whether it's possible to romance Vicki in GTA 6.

Is Vicki romanceable in GTA 6?

Initially, you meet Vicki when playing as Lucia near the start of Chapter 2, which takes place in Kelly County. At this point in the story, Lucia is getting most of the screen time while Jason is unplayable for story reasons we won't spoil.

The pair are holed up in the Starlet Motel for the time being and in need of medication. Lucia finds out that a woman named Vicki at the Starlet Motel apparently sells drugs that can do the trick.

From here, Lucia and Vicki get into all sorts of hijinks together, along with the help of a degenerate named Dunk. You'll eventually finish Vicki's story after a robbery at Delights Cabaret, which is the strip club where Vicki works.

Unfortunately, throughout all of these interactions, it's not possible to romance Vicki at any point in GTA 6. This goes for both Jason and Lucia, as Vicki is seemingly only interested in doing business, not business time.

However, there is a brief interaction you can have with Vicki if you act quickly. Prior to the end of the "Painkiller" mission in GTA 6, which sees Lucia running around trying to get the meds, you can catch a special dance from Vicki at Delights Cabaret. Vicki goes on stage and does a dance, with her clothes on, for the audience at the club. During this point, you'll still be playing as Lucia, so she'll be the one at the club if you see Vicki's dance.

This isn't a romance option for Vicki, as she will dance whether you're there or not, but it is a secret encounter that lets you see more of her character in GTA 6. After the Painkiller mission ends, though, you won't be able to see her dance at Delights again.

If you happened to miss out on Vicki's dance, you can technically see more of her by visiting Snapmatic on your phone. You're also free to call or text Vicki, as she will respond even after chapter 2 ends in GTA 6.

There’s so much more to learn and do in Leonida, so be sure to use our GTA 6 guides hub.

title: Where To Find Bikinis For Lucia And Swimsuits For Jason In GTA 6
summary:
Before the launch of Grand Theft Auto 6, the internet was bombarded with tons of promotional material showcasing sun-scorched beaches and stunning bods. Then, when you start the campaign, you realize that most stores around you don't offer beach attire. So, now, you’re probably wondering where you can buy bikinis and swimsuits in the game. Here's where to get bikinis for Lucia and swimwear for Jason in GTA 6.

In This Article
  • Souvenirs and swimsuits in GTA 6
  • Where to find De’Luge Swimwear and other stores
  • Where to find the USA-themed bikini

Souvenirs and swimsuits in GTA 6

As you explore more of the game world, you’ll discover various clothing shops, including those that sell attire. You can then browse their locations by opening the map’s GTA Index and selecting the Outfits tab. There, you’ll find the Souvenirs and Swimsuits category, though the main downside is that the vast majority of stores sell the former, not the latter. There are, however, a couple of notable exceptions.

Where to find De’Luge Swimwear and other stores

title: GTA 6 Laptop Password Puzzle Guide
summary:
There certainly are plenty of brain teasers in Grand Theft Auto 6. While the vast majority require thorough exploration, a few are found in areas near and dear to you. In fact, certain clues might be hidden in plain sight, too. Here’s how you can solve the laptop puzzle in your apartment.

Note: We don’t want to spoil all the details, but it’s important that you solve this puzzle before you finish chapter 3.

In This Article
  • Laptop password clues
  • Laptop puzzle solution
  • Where to find Auntie’s Place
  • Laptop puzzle rewards

Laptop password clues

The laptop puzzle in GTA 6 is actually located in your Bayside apartment, which you gain access to in chapter 3. In the bedroom, you should see a laptop on the desk with the ring light. If you interact with it, though, you’ll realize that it requires a password.

The clues themselves are also inside the apartment:

  • In the hallway, there’s a memorial photo for a dog named Muffins.
  • On the bedside table, there’s a drawing of Muffins wearing a queen’s crown.
  • If you flip that notepad, the words “Class of ‘15 reunion next Friday” are shown on the back.

Laptop puzzle solution

The clues pertain to the laptop’s password. Interact with the device and choose these options when prompted:

  • Muffins
  • Queen
  • 15

This unlocks the device, allowing you to browse various thirsty messages and raunchy photos. That said, there’s one message that you do need to read.

Go to the WhatUp tab and look for the “Unknown” sender. The text should state the following: “Go to La Perle right next to Auntie’s Place and use 92665 to get it. I think you’re going to really love it.” This is one of the few relatively GTA 6 safe codes that isn't randomized.

Where to find Auntie’s Place

The GTA 6 laptop puzzle refers to “Auntie’s Place.” If you go to the neighborhood of La Perle, you’ll see a restaurant called Aunt Zola’s Soul Food, a popular establishment among Haitians in the community. The restaurant even has a scannable object that helps you unlock the Sniper of La Perle hidden playlist.

To the left of that building, there’s an alley that leads to an abandoned yard. There, you’ll spot a shed. If you look closely, you’ll see that it has a keypad.

Laptop puzzle rewards

Interact with the keypad and enter 9-2-6-6-5. This unlocks the shutter, revealing some nifty rewards:

  • First, there’s the vehicle, a Pfister Growler owned by “Vanessa.” Since this is a unique variant, it counts as a standout option.
  • Second, the shed itself acts as a free garage, allowing you to keep one owned vehicle.
  • Finally, at the back of the shed, there’s a weapon locker for quick loadout swapping when you’re on the go.

These are some pretty nice rewards, wouldn’t you say? Again, be sure to solve the laptop puzzle before completing chapter 3, as you might miss out on these goodies later in the game.

title: Use This GTA 6 Infinite Money Glitch Before It’s Patched
summary:
In Grand Theft Auto 6, Jason and Lucia are on the run from the law and hardened criminals. They can’t just start their own financial empires or rule the seedy underworld of Leonida. They have to scratch and claw their way to the top from one small-time job to the next. But for those who want to see rags turn into riches rather quickly, there’s an exploit that gives you infinite money in the game, around $230,000 or more per attempt, if you play your cards right.

  • The infinite cash exploit: Teddy bear cocaine

The infinite cash exploit: Teddy bear cocaine

The GTA 6 infinite cash exploit involves vans with delightful-looking teddy bear designs. Don’t let the whimsical art fool you, because they actually have packets of cocaine. The location is in an abandoned warehouse in South Vice-Dale County, which is east of Hamlet.

Infinite cash exploit requirements

To be clear, you can do this exploit as early as chapter 1, but it’d be such a waste of time because only Jason is playable at that stage. You might think it’s a good idea to do this in chapter 2, but we suggest holding off. Instead, your best bet is to do this after progressing a bit further into chapter 3.

During chapter 3, you meet an NPC named Tyrone in Vice City. He’s a fence that buys narcotics for a high value. This means you’ll get the most bang for your buck if you sell your drugs to him.

The next step is purely optional, but it does help you gain more money. In any case, you should consider registering at least one delivery van with 10 slots.

  • Examples include the DeClasse Burrito ‘98, Brute Boxville, Vapid Rumpo, or Vapid Shifter. Here are some additional tidbits:
  • You need to have at least one vacant garage so you can register this extra vehicle.
  • Alternatively, any other vehicle with enough storage in the trunk would do.

The teddy bear drug warehouse

Anyway, your goal now is to make your way to the aforementioned warehouse on the map pictured earlier in our guide.

  • Make sure your active character is alone. If you’re playing as Jason, you should tell Lucia that you want to “split up.” Your inactive character should go somewhere else automatically.
  • Next, mark the warehouse’s location on your map and use the RydeMe app to save time.
  • Just outside the warehouse, you’ll spot several vans (including those with 10 slots), as well as one van with the teddy bear design. Open the back and pick up three packs of cocaine.
  • Then, go inside the warehouse. If it’s your first time visiting this location, you’ll see several dead bodies, as well as stacks of marked money. There’s even a collectible card in the office room.
  • In the warehouse, there’s also a second teddy bear van with three packs of cocaine. Make sure to grab those.
  • Assuming your two stash bags are full--i.e. each one has more than $10,000--you can place them in the back of the other van in the area (not the one with the teddy bear design).

How to do the infinite money exploit

Here’s where the magic happens.Mmake sure you’re outside the warehouse with your active character. Then, switch to your inactive character quickly, before switching back to your active character.

Assuming your other character is in a distant area, the mere act of swapping causes objects in the location to respawn. The six cocaine packets will be back inside the vans once more. However, the corpses of the drug runners and the marked money won’t be around. That’s totally fine because we can still rake in a lot of dough.

Go ahead and pick up all the drugs. Again, take note of how much money you have, which is seen in the upper-right corner of the screen:

  • Each packet of cocaine nets you $1,200.
  • A full run outside and inside the warehouse nets you $7,200.
  • Swap to your inactive character, then swap back to your active character. Then, pick up more narcotics.
  • Your character can carry two large stash bags, and each one should have around $10,600. With two full bags, you’ll have $21,600. Place both bags in the trunk of the van once they’re completely full.
  • Since the van outside has 10 slots, the total amount is $106,000.

Now, you might think that more than 100k sounds great, but we can get extra moolah. We've outlined the steps below.

How to use your partner to maximize your monetary gains

We’re going to go the distance here to rake in the dough. Let’s say one of the non-teddy bear vans already has full slots. Here’s what you need to do next:

  • Remember the delivery van that you registered? Use the ScooterBros app to have it delivered to your location. From this point onward, keep doing the character-switching method.
  • Now, you’ve got another van that can store 10 more stash bags. That’s an extra $106,000. (If you pick a different vehicle, that’s still fine. You just need the storage space anyway.)
  • Once both vans are filled to the brim, do more character switches until both bags that you’re carrying are full. Drop them on the ground.
  • Do more character switches until you have another two bags that are also full.
  • Next, tell your partner to “meet up” with you. They’ll use RydeMe to arrive at your location. Give them a kiss if you'd like… and two of the bags, more importantly.
  • Your active character can carry the remaining bags on their own.

This next part is important for the infinite money cheat in GTA 6:

  • Highlight your inactive character but don’t switch to them. Instead, tell them that they should drive. This will cause them to drive the personal vehicle that you had delivered (including all the bags inside).
  • As for your active character, you can drive the first van that you’ve been using as storage.
  • Open the character panel again and select “follow me” to have your partner drive behind you. An example of this can be seen in the image above.
  • Travel all the way to Tyrone’s apartment and park both vans/vehicles in the nearby lot. You should be able to sell your entire haul in one go.

All in all, we’ve got 20 bags inside two vans, as well as four bags carried by Jason and Lucia. These 24 bags, assuming you got the maximum amount of coke packets, should net you a whopping $254,400 in just 10 to 15 minutes.

Best of all, you saved a bit of time since, instead of traveling back and forth with a smaller haul, you got more than double the amount and made only one trip. Keep repeating the GTA 6 infinite money glitch so you can swim in riches.

Note: Last but not least, it’s worth mentioning that all your transactions with Tyrone might be left on “pending” status if your BuckMe bank account’s credit limit hasn’t increased yet. You need to complete main missions until you reach a new tier. All the money you’ve amassed will still be sent to you later on, so don’t worry.

title: This GTA 6 Glitch (Almost) Ruined The Game’s Most Iconic Scene
summary:
Note: This story will discuss a pivotal mission in Chapter 2 of Grand Theft Auto 6.

A powerful sequence in Grand Theft Auto 6 is quickly becoming a favorite among the game's many players, but a technical mishap made my experience of this scene very different--hilariously different.

Chapter 2 of GTA 6 begins with Jason and Lucia in a rough spot, with the former still recovering from major injuries sustained at the end of Chapter 1, and the latter having to care for him. It isn't until the mission "Breakfast Run" that Jason is back on his feet, and the Bonnie-and-Clyde-like duo mark his recovery with a crime spree.

Set to "Money or Nothing" by Dire Straits, Lucia and Jason rob a diner, not dissimilar to a scene from Pulp Fiction, and a playable montage shows the pair robbing convenience shops, a clothing store, and other establishments. The image of Jason and Lucia busting open double doors, guns in hand, is probably the most iconic image of GTA 6, a statement of intent that defines the game's story going forward.

But somehow, I had gotten a slightly different version of this montage. When I returned to the motel as Lucia, I sprinted toward the door, only for the game to place me back outside the room. The game told me to "Go to Hank's Waffles" with no additional context, and I walked back into the motel to find Jason, not only up and about, but only sporting his underwear, bandages, and a buzz cut.

I suspected that there was a cutscene that I missed showing Jason fully recovered, so I decided to carry out the mission. The problem was that Jason wouldn't put any clothes on. I drove to the diner as the game instructed me to, and the entire mission, Dire Straits and all, resumed with a mostly naked Jason.

It was impossible not to cackle at the sheer absurdity of the situation, watching Jason terrorize locals and presumably solidifying a new legacy as the Leonida underwear robber. At one point, the camera cut to Jason's bare foot slamming a gas pedal, and I was left breathless from laughter. Eventually, the game decided to put clothes back on Jason, but I had to visit a salon to grow his hair back.

Though GTA 6 features nudity in various degrees, you cannot dress Jason and Lucia in their underwear outside of their home. That sprint through the motel room door must have bypassed some sort of clothing check and allowed Jason to freely show skin outside of the motel. I've seen players online talk about an "underwear glitch," and I found one Reddit comment saying that they also had a nearly naked Jason run about in "Breakfast Run," so I appear to be an edge case in experiencing this specific glitch.

I can't say that this bug "ruined" one of GTA 6's best missions for me, as I still found myself thoroughly entertained--just not in the way Rockstar Games wanted. Having Jason in his undies while still concealing his identity with a hat and bandana felt like something out of a Saints Row game rather than the fairly serious story GTA 6 was building up to that point.

Despite the intense work and detail put into GTA 6, it certainly isn't free of silly glitches and bugs such as this. Luckily, many of them are more amusing than hampering, and Rockstar Games is already putting out post-launch patches for the title. If anything, I'm just bummed that I can't spend the rest of the game as Underwear Jason.

title: GTA 6 Online Could Be Bigger Than Fortnite, Bank Of America Stock Analyst Says
summary:
Rockstar Games and parent company Take-Two are riding high currently from the success of Grand Theft Auto 6 with a reported 45 million copies sold and $4 billion in revenue already, but this could just the beginning of how much money GTA 6 could bring in. According to Bank of America stock analyst Omar Dessouky, the initial success of GTA 6 reinforces the company's belief that the game has a massive reach, and with that comes the possibility of monetizing the players even more when the next evolution of GTA Online is released.

In fact, SeekingAlpha reported that Dessouky said he is so bullish that he believes GTA Online alone "can become a multibillion-dollar franchise, potentially larger than Fortnite." He said Fortnite generates as much as $5 billion in annual revenue, and GTA Online could be bigger in the fullness of time.

The stock analyst went on to raise his price target on Take-Two's stock to $350. That would represent a significant upside, considering Take-Two currently trades at around $210/share.

Take-Two's stock got hammered in 2026 and never fully recovered. The company's shares are down 16% so far in 2026 and down 12% over the past year.

Investing is a long-term game, though. Zooming out, Take-Two has crushed it since GTA 5 released. If you bought $10,000 worth of Take-Two stock on the day GTA 5 came out in 2013, and never sold, you'd have more than $120,000 today.

As for the next iteration of GTA Online, Rockstar has not said a word about what to expect or if such a mode is even coming. GTA 6, after all, is marketed as a strictly single-player game.

That being said, it seems plainly obvious that a new version of GTA Online is coming. According to multiple reports, the new version of GTA Online for GTA 6 could launch in 2027, along with a PC edition of the game.

GTA Online for GTA 5 has been, and continues to this day, to be a major moneymaker for Rockstar and Take-Two, and it's expected that the developer will find even more ways to make money from players with GTA 6 Online. Some have theorized that GTA 6 Online could have some form of user-generated content, for example, potentially leading to a marketplace of some kind.

GTA 6 launched on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S, and it reached 32.5 million copies sold via pre-purchases alone. On day one, GTA 6 generated $3.79 billion in revenue. Over the first four days, GTA 6 has climbed to 44.9 million copies sold and more than $4 billion in revenue, according to a report.

For more, check out GameSpot’s GTA 6 review. If you’re just getting started with the game, be sure to read GameSpot’s top five best things to do first.

title: All Airports In GTA 6
summary:
Some points of interest are more important than others in Grand Theft Auto 6, and airports are always at the top of a player's list of places to see. While airports often play a critical role in a GTA story, they're also useful for knowing where planes are located on the map. We've already covered how to get a plane and other aircraft in GTA 6, but airports are different.

Whether you're looking to steal a plane or land one so you can keep it hidden in a hangar, GTA 6 has several airports and airfields you need to know about. You can see where they're located in Leonida in the guide below.

All airport and airfield locations in GTA 6

There are a few specifically named airports and airfields in Leonida that you'll eventually learn about through the main story. However, the map also features unnamed locations that function as airfields you can use whenever you please. These are much harder to find, but we've scoured the map to locate each one.

Below, you'll see the complete list of airports and airfields along with their precise locations in GTA 6.

Vice City International Airport

This is the largest and most obvious airport in GTA 6. VCIA is located right in the middle of Leonida (west Vice-Dale County) and plays a key role in the main story. While you'll visit here a few times during the story, you're also free to break into the airport, inside and out, to see everything it contains. Be warned, though, as breaking into the exterior of VCIA gives you an immediate three- or four-star Wanted level.

Mile Zero Air Station

This is the other major airport in GTA 6, but unlike VCIA, Mile Zero Air Station doesn't fly commuters out of the city. Instead, the air station is a military base that houses fighter jets, tanks, and armored vehicles. The base is extremely difficult to break into, and you'll be swarmed by guards if you're caught here. However, it's a high-risk, high-reward location that allows you to drive some of the best vehicles in the game. You can find Mile Zero Air Station west of Key Lento, hidden away in the southwestern part of the map.

Wild Hog Point

This is the only named airfield in GTA 6, and you'll eventually see it by playing through Pilot Pete's side questline. There are free planes for the taking all over Wild Hog Point, and it's fairly easy to get to during Chapter 2. If you're in Key Lento or Vice City, though, it's quite the drive, as you'll find it in northern Kelly County, southwest of Port Gellhorn.

Watson Bay Airport

Next up is the Watson Bay Airport, which you can find west of Watson Bay and south of Bobcat Key in Mariana County. Not much goes on at this location, but it can be a great spot to evade police, as there's only a single road that goes in and out of the airport.

Mariana County Airfield

Once again, there's an unnamed airfield in Mariana County that you won't see much of in GTA 6. However, this airfield comes into play during Pilot Pete's questline, and it's more central than Watson Bay Airport. You'll also find Paradise Garage nearby, giving you an easy spot to store a vehicle for a quick getaway.

LTF Airfield

This is the final airfield in Mariana County, and it's tucked between the Leonida Keys and Grassrivers regions. LTF Airfield doesn't have much to see, but there are some spare planes you can take if you want to head to the skies for sightseeing or use a parachute in GTA 6.

Leonard County Airfield

We're heading north to Leonard County, and this airfield is situated just north of Bellville. On the map, this doesn't look like an airfield, but rather another subdivision for the Cellerica cult in GTA 6. However, it's an active airfield that just doesn't see much use during your travels in Leonida.

Sundown Private Airfield

The Sundown Private Airfield is located in Leonard County, just west of Waning Sands. Despite being called a private airfield, we never found a massive amount of security that would take you down for being there. Still, if you're looking to be stealthy, you might want to try another airfield.

Ambrosia Airfield

Ambrosia isn't filled to the brim with sights to see, but it does have an airfield that's fairly central to other regions in Leonida. The airfield is a bit desolate, but that just means you'll likely be the only person there most of the time. You'll find it west of Ambrosia and south of Frogswater.

Kelly County Airfield

In addition to Wild Hog Point, Kelly County has another airfield that's located just below the Lummox County border and Mount Kalaga National Park. This airfield is easy to miss if you're on the other side of Mount Kalaga, but it has some great views of the mountain when landing or flying out of it.

Lummox County Airfield

Finally, we have the Lummox County Airfield, which is in the middle of nowhere in the northern part of the region. There's no real reason for you to visit this part of the map, but you can head in if you're looking to do some nearby hunting in GTA 6 and don't want to drive through Lummox County.

And that does it for all of the known airports and airfields in GTA 6. As time goes on, more airfields might be discovered, but this is all we know about for now.

There’s so much more to learn and do in Leonida, so be sure to use our GTA 6 guides hub.

title: After The Ocarina Of Time Remake, I Finally Forgive Navi
summary:
I used to firmly believe that Navi from the original Ocarina of Time ruined video games. It’s a completely exaggerated and unscientific take; tutorialization and annoying characters have always existed in the medium. But every time a modern video game character gives me unsolicited verbal advice, or when the protagonist I’m playing as mutters a puzzle solution to themselves, or passive-aggressively suggests where I should go next--short of breaking the fourth wall and looking at me through the TV screen like I’m an idiot--I think of Navi.

While I doubt that Navi directly inspired this game-design precedent that modern AAA games employ far too often, I do think that The Legend of Zelda’s seminal “annoying sidekick” set a precedent for how games disseminate information to the player. Ocarina of Time rightfully receives credit for its influence on how 3D video games are built and how players navigate through 3D spaces. At the same time, I see Ocarina as the beginning of a trend where grating, unskippable, and unavoidable tutorials come in the form of an actual character.

At the time, Navi was a necessity--Shigeru Miyamoto, despite having problems with Navi, admitted so, saying that the game would be “unfriendly to players” without her hints. Gaming technology had advanced significantly, and 3D environments were still a relatively new frontier; help was needed, especially for children or less experienced players. But that doesn’t cancel out the irritation that Navi would spark when she interrupts your gameplay, and the condescension that comes across when she explains what to do as you’re about to do it. The infamous pestering voice clips of “Hey!” and “Listen!” certainly didn’t help.

Going into the Ocarina of Time remake with these strong feelings, I admit that I’m surprised I came out after rolling credits not just being fine with Navi, but actually liking her quite a bit. Many of the pain points from the original game were addressed one way or another. For one, Navi wasn’t interrupting gameplay to chime in; the only time you really hear from her in actual gameplay is when you manually press right on the D-pad to receive hints about enemies and certain environmental elements. Her most useful in-game function felt more like a deliberate choice that players could make.

But to my surprise, Navi felt like a fully realized character in the remake. Voice acting in cutscenes and the higher production value certainly made this possible. Thanks to added dialogue, Navi feels like a proper companion character to Link, emoting and speaking for him when this silent protagonist obviously cannot. Navi carries much of the weight in conversations with NPCs like the Great Deku Tree and the Sages, advocating for Link and moving exposition along at a nice pace. 

I think about the gag when the game’s central Goron character, Darunia, congratulates Link, aggressively patting him on the head and accidentally knocking him out. In the original game, Navi floats around with no reaction, as usual. In the remake, Navi not only checks up on Link, but lightly chastises the bulked-up Goron (“Hey! You’re too strong for your own good, Darunia!”).

Navi is still chatty in the remake, but Nintendo was wise to make much of her in-game dialogue relayed through speech bubbles, and instead of patronizing tips, they are observations and exclamations that reflect Navi’s curious-but-sometimes-childish personality. Aesthetically, I appreciate that Navi, usually depicted as a plain orb of light, has texture, as though she’s covered in some kind of fuzz.

The remake’s approach to Navi encapsulates all the changes and “improvements” made in the Switch 2 game: Everyone’s look has evolved, either drastically or subtly, still containing the essence of the original designs but given additional detail. And personality-wise, everyone is a lot more colorful, while still staying true to their original characters. It’s changes like these that make all the characters, Navi included, feel more tangible and grounded, which only helps make the Ocarina of Time remake feel more immersive.

This revised Navi still left a little to be desired; I wish I had the ability to prompt Navi to give a hint when I needed it, or at least be able to talk to her the same way you could for Midna in Twilight Princess or even Fi in Skyward Sword. Regardless, Navi turned from a tooltip regurgitator to a real character. If Nintendo could learn how to fix Navi, then hopefully other blockbuster games could do the same for their own talkative, annoying sidekicks.

title: Grand Theft Auto 6’s HDR Is Broken, But These Tweaks Can Fix It
summary:
Grand Theft Auto VI is a visual and audial treat, and is easily one of the most technically impressive games on the current generation of consoles. But it isn't without issues, especially if you're trying to experience the sights and sounds of Vice City with all the moody contrast and bright highlights that HDR offers.

That's due to an HDR calibration tool that isn't exactly working in the way that you expect it. Like many other games, GTA VI doesn't use the system-level HDR settings on either the PlayStation 5 or Xbox Series X|S. Instead it features its own calibration tool, which lets you adjust the maximum brightness, black levels, and paper white values that work best on your display. While the tool makes calibration seem straightforward, there's an issue with it that makes it very unreliable.

Specifically, the maximum brightness and paper white point values seem to be linked in a way that is both unclear and incorrect. Normally you would set these values individually, with maximum brightness set according to the value your display supports and the paper white value that looks best to you. GTA VI instead changes the maximum peak brightness value it is storing as you change the paper white point. For example, if you set a maximum peak brightness at 1000 nits (a typical value) but then reduce the paper white point (given how how its default is), the peak brightness value reduces as well, with no indication to you that it's happening.

HDR enthusiasts and handy calibration assistors HDTVTest and GamingTech have both confirmed the issue, and provided some rough workarounds until Rockstar (hopefully) releases a fix. The idea is setting the maximum brightness value higher than your display supports, but in line with what the game is expecting based on the paper white point value to choose. It's confusing, but GamingTech has drawn up a table that might help depending on your display's specifications. That's due to an HDR calibration tool that isn't exactly working in the way that you expect it.
